title: Weekly SAT Learning Report (Period Ending 2026-08-06)
executiveSummary: During the 7-day period ending 2026-08-06, the learner completed 1 diagnostic session (cf15003d-c6f5-438c-bf0f-fdb24d8a5841) comprising 12 items (11 Reading & Writing, 1 Math). The learner achieved 100% accuracy (12/12) with rapid pacing averaging 17s per item (well below the target average of 60s). While baseline competence at Difficulty Level 2 is clear across all tested skills, significant under-confidence was recorded, with 7 of 12 items marked as 'unsure' (6) or 'guessing' (1). Because each skill has only 1 attempt in a single session, skills cannot yet be classified as fluent, mastered, or retained. Immediate escalation to Difficulty Level 3 and expansion of Math skill coverage are recommended.

limitations: All evidence derives from a single diagnostic session (cf15003d-c6f5-438c-bf0f-fdb24d8a5841) conducted on 2026-08-06.
Sample size per skill is N=1, preventing definitive assessment of skill mastery, stability, or transfer.
Math domain is severely under-sampled (1 algebra question only), leaving non-linear algebra, problem solving, geometry, and trigonometry unassessed.
No multi-session longitudinal data exists to evaluate retention over time.

Learner's rapid completion times (9s-18s on grammar/transitions) suggest strong intuitive mastery, but lack of rule awareness drives self-doubt.
